description:
Sanctioned, PEP, state-owned and restricted parties near an organization or person,
each with its markers and the path to it: who holds what in whom at every step.

Polixis returns the network around the entity, both its smart graph and its full graph
with signatories, third parties and historic ties. This MCP picks the parties whose flags
or alerts carry a risk marker and finds a shortest path to each over Polixis's links.

Use it for PEP and state-ownership exposure nearby; for sanctions at any distance use
`get_sanctions_exposure`. `total_by_risk` counts every flagged party by marker across
every page, and every page repeats it, so a question such as "is any of them
state-owned?" is settled by a 0 there. The most severe come first: sanctioned, then PEP,
then restricted or in a sanction-sensitive territory, then former PEP or REP, and
state-owned last; the nearest first within each. So stop once the risks are milder than
the question cares about.
When `truncated_by_polixis` is true, Polixis cut the network short: do not report that
none was found. When `next_cursor` is set, pass it back as `cursor` for the next page.

description:
Companies an organization or person is tied to: directly, as owner, director, signatory
or subsidiary, or through people in between, such as a PEP's relative or associate, or a
director or owner the company shares with it. Each comes with the chains of people and the
links that tie it, and its flags.

Polixis returns the network around the entity: with `scope` key its smart graph, which
leaves out signatory, third-party and historic relations, and with `all` its full graph
too. This MCP finds the companies in it and the chains of people that tie each one.

The nearest come first, then the flagged, then those tied through the most people, so the
first page usually answers the question, and `total_by_risk` counts the flagged companies
by marker. When `truncated_by_polixis` is true, Polixis cut the network short, so more
companies may exist. Start with `radius` 2 and widen to 3 only when the
question needs ties further out. For what an entity owns down the chain use
`get_top_down_ownership`; for sanctioned, PEP or state-owned parties
`find_flagged_parties`. When `next_cursor` is set, pass it back as `cursor`.

radius.description: Links out from the entity to look. 2 finds the companies tied to it directly or through one person; 3 also those tied through two people in a row, such as a relative's business partner. Polixis documents no maximum and stopped at 2 in every walk we tried, so 3 may find nothing more, from a much larger graph.

The directors, executives, signatories, shareholders, holdings and other parties
related to an organization or person, with their roles, shares, dates, sources and flags.

Each party comes once, with the relations every source reports; those with a current
relation come first. When `next_cursor` is set, pass it back as `cursor` for the next

`get_ultimate_beneficial_owners` instead.

description:

shareholdings reach it, with the share the entity carries in it summed over every chain,
the chain carrying the most, and its flags.

Polixis traces the tree down through subsidiaries and shareholding layers, and reports
the role and share of each link only. This MCP turns the tree into rows and computes the

minority stakes trail: stop once you have what the question needs. When `next_cursor`

description:
Who owns or controls an organization: one row per owner, however many chains reach it,
with the share it carries in the organization summed over every chain, the chain carrying
the most, and its flags.

Polixis traces the tree up through shareholders and control layers to the last owners,
and reports the role and share of each link only. This MCP turns the tree into rows and

others carry their flags on their own rows.

Rows come largest effective share first, so a threshold question such as "who holds 25%
or more" is settled once the shares fall below it: stop there rather than reading every
page, unless `total_share_unknown` counts owners not yet read, whose share may be higher.

description: Checks a pid the user already holds, such as one stored in a client file. Call it first whenever the user gives a pid rather than a name. `status` is `active` when the pid is current: use it as it is. It is `merged` when Polixis merged the entity into another, whose pid is `redir`: use that one, and tell the user to update their records. It is `never minted` when Polixis does not know the pid, which Polixis's documentation calls `unknown`: say so, describe no entity, and find the client again by name or identifier. An HTTP error 410 means the pid named a group Polixis dissolved, and its body lists the former members.

description:
Find organizations and people in Polixis by name or identifier, with their sanctions and
PEP flags, dates, countries and identifiers to tell matches apart. Vessels and aircraft are
organizations here.

Call it first when you have a name or identifier: every other Polixis tool takes a match's
`pid`. When the user gives a pid instead, call `resolve_permanent_id` with it. A match may
not show that a person is a former PEP: before saying a person is not a PEP, read the
`flags` of `get_entity_profiles`, which show FORMER_PEP. When `next_cursor` is set, more
matches exist: pass it back as `cursor` to page through them.

A match needs a date that fits one of them: a year takes any date in it, a month any day in it, and a full date also takes a record that knows only its month or year. Polixis filters on it, so it narrows a common name better than comparing the matches yourself.
